summary: Iteration 17 — forgot_password LOCKOUT FIX VERIFIED. Static code review of /app/backend/routes/auth.py forgot_password (lines 308-367) confirms the correct order: (1) lookup user, (2) generate temp password in memory only, (3) call send_email(...), (4) if send_email returns falsy -> raise HTTPException(500) with Turkish detail 'E-posta gönderilemedi, şifreniz değiştirilmedi...' and NO UPDATE runs, (5) only after send_email succeeds does the UPDATE users SET password=..., must_change_password=1 execute. There is no code path that mutates users.password when send_email fails. Live end-to-end proof against https://price-update-test.preview.emergentagent.com: POST /api/auth/forgot-password with cakmak_ebubekir@hotmail.com returned 500 with detail containing 'şifreniz değiştirilmedi'; POST /api/auth/login with the same account + 'admin' returned 200 with access_token immediately after — repeated the pair twice (idempotence proven). Unknown email 'yok@example.com' → 200 generic (no enumeration). Empty email → 400. Pytest: 7/8 PASS. The single FAIL is unrelated to this fix — regression login cakmak.ebubekir29@gmail.com / 1234567 returned 401 'şifre hatalı'; this credential in /app/memory/test_credentials.md appears stale (this account's password was likely rotated externally by the user; the current forgot_password change does NOT touch login logic at all and the hotmail account confirms passwords are NOT being mutated by the fix).

Password was likely rotated by the user directly on the production MySQL. This is NOT caused by the forgot_password change (that path does not modify login or the gmail account in this test run). Ask user to confirm/refresh this credential.

critical_code_review_comments: auth.py:302-305 has a dead-code line — after `return TokenResponse(...)` at line 302, line 305 repeats the same return statement. Unreachable, but harmless. Consider removing.

forgot_password order (auth.py:308-367) matches the integration playbook exactly: temp password is only persisted to MySQL after send_email returns truthy. UPDATE happens in a separate `async with pool.acquire()` block, guaranteed to execute AFTER the send. Good.
Enumeration protection is correct: unknown/inactive user returns a generic 200 message; only KNOWN active users can trigger the 500 path.

send_email(...) call at line 354 is synchronous inside an async endpoint — if the SMTP call blocks it could stall the event loop for the request. Not urgent, but consider running_in_threadpool or an async SMTP client if latency becomes an issue with a real provider.

success_rate.backend: 87.5% (7/8 — 1 fail is stale credential, not fix regression)

rca_of_issue: Original bug (already fixed by main agent): forgot_password UPDATE-then-send order — a failed email would leave the user with a randomly-generated password they never received, locking them out. Fix moves UPDATE strictly after a truthy send_email(...) return; on failure the endpoint raises 500 with a Turkish message and the users row is untouched. Verified live: cakmak_ebubekir@hotmail.com password 'admin' still logs in immediately after two consecutive failed forgot-password calls.
